questions.prompt: Which of these is a warning sign of an unsafe driver?
choices: Adding a mirror on the right side.
One close call in several years.
questions.explanation: Warning signs include getting lost in familiar places, new dents and scrapes, and frequent close calls or collisions.

questions.prompt: An older driver who sees poorly at night must drive after dark. What does the handbook suggest?
choices: Use high beams the whole way.
Drive faster to shorten the trip.
questions.explanation: Seniors may limit night driving and, when they must drive at night, choose a well-lit route.

questions.prompt: Which of these changes can help an older driver stay safe?
choices: Driving at rush hour, when others are alert.
questions.explanation: Seniors may drive when traffic is light, avoid difficult intersections and freeways, keep trips short, and add a right-side mirror.

questions.prompt: What happens to the driving ability of a person with progressive dementia?
choices: In time, they can no longer drive safely.
It stays steady if they keep driving often.
It returns once they start taking medicine.
questions.explanation: People with progressive dementia ultimately lose the ability to drive safely, and caregivers, doctors or police often must stop them.
